teams.heading: Fiji suffer third straight Nations Championship loss after falling to Scotland
teams.body: Fiji are seeking a reset after a 17-33 defeat against Scotland in round three of the Nations Championship. That result leaves Fiji bottom of the table, sitting twelfth of 12 teams after three matches. Their next opponents are France, who defeated Fiji 34-21 in their last meeting in November 2025. Across their first three tournament fixtures, the team have conceded 145 points. Meanwhile, Fiji have managed to score only 49 points in those same three matches.

teams.heading: Eddie Hearn faces reality check over Henry Pollock’s million pound demand
teams.body: Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn is seeking a £1 million annual contract for Northampton Saints and England back-rower Henry Pollock. The 21-year-old, who toured with the British and Irish Lions after earning 13 senior caps, is currently on a deal worth roughly £150,000. While Pollock is among the 25 players recently awarded enhanced elite player contracts by Steve Borthwick, England veterans Ben Youngs and Dan Cole warned Hearn that rugby lacks the "Riyadh" riches of boxing to meet such a valuation.

lead.why: The entry of celebrity promoter Eddie Hearn into rugby player management and his audacious financial demands for Henry Pollock is the day's most discussed storyline.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié's France bolster scoring average following 42-15 Japan win
teams.body: France go into the Nations Championship break third in the standings, having maintained a prolific scoring rate of 38.7 points per game across their last 11 matches. During this period, the national side has scored 426 points and conceded 291, an average of 26.5 per fixture. This clinical streak includes a 54-12 victory away to Wales in February, the largest winning margin of the window. Following the 42-15 win against Japan, the squad sits behind only the top two on points difference.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out of Ireland’s November tests with vascular injury
teams.body: Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley will miss the November international window as he continues to recover from a vascular injury. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan confirmed the 35-cap playmaker is unlikely to feature until the new year, ruling him out of the upcoming test against Argentina and subsequent clashes with Fiji and South Africa. Crowley previously missed the July series after playing every minute of Ireland’s 2024 Triple Crown-winning campaign. McMillan noted that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority" for the 26-year-old.

lead.why: Jack Crowley is Ireland's starting fly-half and his confirmed absence through 2026 significantly impacts the November test window.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby faces legal battle as High Court allows brain injury claims
teams.body: The legal proceedings brought by roughly 500 former players over neurological injuries remain active following a High Court ruling earlier this month. The court rejected a bid by World Rugby and the British governing bodies—including Scottish Rugby—to have the concussion-related lawsuits dismissed. While the decision ensures the cases proceed toward trial, the litigation remains unresolved. The sport continues to navigate the long-term implications of these historical claims as the governing bodies prepare their next steps in the landmark case.

teams.heading: Wales mourns iconic sporting figure Sir Billy Boston aged 92
teams.body: Sir Billy Boston has died at the age of 92, just days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan. A Cardiff-born icon who represented Neath and Pontypridd in the early 1950s, he later became a titan of rugby league during his 15-year tenure at Wigan. The Welsh Rugby Union paid tribute to the former Great Britain star, describing him as "one of the best loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport" following his passing in Wigan.

lead.why: The passing of Sir Billy Boston is a significant moment in Welsh sporting history that transcends individual rugby codes.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi names unchanged Argentina XV to face visiting Wallabies side
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has kept faith with the starting side that pushed the Springboks close in their recent encounter, opting for an unchanged XV for the opening Test against Australia. While the run-on group remains static, the head coach has adjusted his matchday 23 by shifting to a 5:3 bench split. Captain Pablo Matera continues to lead the pack in the ongoing absence of Julián Montoya, who remains unavailable for this fixture alongside several other senior squad members.

teams.heading: Les Kiss rotates forward pack and omits Harry Wilson for Argentina
teams.body: Coach Les Kiss has overhauled his forward pack for the upcoming test against Argentina, omitting captain Harry Wilson entirely as part of a strategic push to build squad depth ahead of next year’s World Cup. Allan Alaalatoa takes over the captaincy, while Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii begins on the bench. Kiss noted that the reshaped pack is “worthwhile exploring” to ensure the team can “raise that competitive dial” and eventually field two competitive starting XVs as the 2027 tournament approaches.

lead.why: The squad rotation and the surprise omission of captain Harry Wilson for the Argentina test is the most significant tactical news today.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One settles legal dispute over player registration rules
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has revised its controversial eligibility criteria following a legal challenge from 24 players. The league confirmed it will allow naturalised players who held citizenship by May 2025 to retain their registration status, averting potential exclusion from domestic squads. Additionally, the JRLO introduced a special measure reclassifying Brave Blossoms with 30 or more caps from Category A-2 to A-1. The governing body admitted that previous communication regarding these system changes was insufficient, prompting the settlement.

lead.why: The resolution of the high-profile legal dispute regarding JRLO player eligibility rules marks a significant shift in domestic rugby policy.

teams.heading: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu replaces Handré Pollard for South Africa against New Zealand
teams.body: New Zealand prepare for a shifted tactical challenge in Cape Town after South Africa confirmed a late change at fly-half. Handré Pollard has been ruled out of the second Test after failing a fitness test on a training injury. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who started in the Springboks’ 33-16 defeat at Ellis Park, moves into the starting side. While Pollard offered set-piece reliability, Rassie Erasmus now turns to the more adventurous Feinberg-Mngomezulu as the hosts look to level the series.

lead.why: The late change to South Africa's starting fly-half directly impacts New Zealand's tactical preparation for the upcoming Test.
